To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a simple and structured method for identifying LH lesions is feasible in routine practice and that a specific training allows inexperienced health care providers to acquire high diagnostic performance in identifying LH lesions.
a structured and well codified method of palpation allows to identify skin LH lesions in insulin-treated PWD with a high accuracy and a very good consistency among HPs.
a suitable training allows HPs to identify LH lesions in insulin-treated diabetic patients with high accuracy and consistency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a method allowing health professionals to identify lipohypertrophy lesions as inexpensively as possible and with high diagnostic accuracy.
the development of a new diagnostic tool for the identification of LH lesions.
the development and validation of a method to identify LH lesions in insulin-treated patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a structured method for the detection of LH lesions is feasible, reliable, and cost effective.
a simple, well codified, and structured palpation technique allows the detection of skin LH lesions as correctly and inexpensively as ultrasound scan.
a structured palpation method allows HPs to identify LH lesions with the same accuracy as USS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a suitable palpation technique can be learned by health professionals and that it can allow them to identify skin lipodystrophic lesions in insulin treated patients with diabetes.
a suitable palpation technique can be taught to health professionals and allows them to identify skin lipodystrophic lesions in insulin-injected areas of people with diabetes.
the simple and inexpensive procedure described here allows HPs to identify LH lesions with the same accuracy as USS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of LH lesions is feasible with the right training.
a structured method allows HPs to correctly identify LH lesions as easily and inexpensively as possible.
a suitable palpation technique is a simple and effective way to identify LH lesions.
